title: Next.js Rendering & Caching: Static, Dynamic, Revalidation & Per-User Data
concept: Choose how every page renders and what it may cache: static, revalidated or dynamic rendering, server and client components, cache keys that never mix users, revalidation by tag after an edit, stale-while-revalidate, and personal data kept out of shared caches.
description: An intermediate course for React developers who build with the Next.js App Router and need pages that are fast without being wrong. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform - a learner who saw another learner's progress on the dashboard, a course page that kept the old price after an instructor edited it, a hydration error that only happened in Vietnamese, a whole page that went dynamic because of one cookie read, a client bundle that grew because a chart became a client component - and fixes it with a decision you can check: static, ISR or dynamic rendering, server or client components, hydration, safe cache keys, the Stale Page or Data Leak scenario, TTL and stale-while-revalidate, revalidation by tag and path, splitting public and personal data, dynamic routes, streaming with Suspense and debugging the cache in production. 12 lessons with True/False quizzes on real code, headers and logs, and TypeScript challenges graded by hidden tests.

learningOutcomes.text: Choose static, revalidated or dynamic rendering for each route from its data and freshness needs
Decide what runs as a server component and what must be a client component, and read hydration errors
Design cache keys that include every input that changes the result, and never mix users
Revalidate by tag or path after a change and use TTL with stale-while-revalidate deliberately
Keep per-user data out of shared caches by splitting public and personal data

testedVersions.Next.js: 16 App Router (lesson examples; caching APIs change between versions, check the docs)

knownIssues: No Next.js in the code runner: challenges model rendering and cache decisions as pure functions and a cache on a fake clock
